text: Withdrawal from addiction treatment is a frequent but difficult-to-predict contingency. We clarify and contextualize the concept of dropouts in addiction treatment, as well as the external and internal elements that most frequently lead to such dropouts. The main instruments used to measure dropout are summarized, after which a new tool, Predictors of Dropout from Addiction Treatment (PDAT) scale, is presented. The PDAT consists of four factors: 1) Motivation: desire to recover and to actively engage in current treatment; 2) Craving: longing for the use of substances and/or the substance addiction environment; 3) Problem awareness: level of insight, or degree of knowledge, and ability to objectify the problem and the disease, with the renunciations and limitations that this entails; and 4) Dysphoria: dyade inner restlessness – moodiness, i.e., emotional disturbance and depressive anticipation that precedes treatment withdrawal.
source_label: Prediction of therapeutic dropout in patients with addictions: Development and validation of the Predictors of Dropout from Addiction Treatment (PDAT) scale
